objective: Add provider-neutral fail-closed artifact lineage and refinement admission that preserves terminal task immutability, parent/child artifact identity, context continuity, scope attenuation, monotonic versions, acceptance evidence, generation and expiry fences, replay/tamper protection, and non-authority boundaries.

research_inputs.finding: A2A v1.0 defines asynchronous task operations, lifecycle, cancellation, idempotency, capability validation, context/task identifiers, artifact exchange, and authentication/authorization objects for opaque agent collaboration.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL models task/artifact lineage and admission evidence without creating tasks, invoking agents, or implementing a network protocol binding.

research_inputs.finding: Terminal tasks are immutable and cannot restart; refinements create new tasks in the same context; artifact references and version history are needed to avoid ambiguity and track mutation.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL requires terminal parent tasks, accepted or superseded parent artifacts, same-context child refinement, monotonic artifact version, stable artifact name, and explicit acceptance evidence.

research_inputs.finding: Durable agent runtimes checkpoint state transitions and resume after failures while separating deterministic workflow control from agent-directed loops.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL keeps refinement admission and lineage evidence separate from task execution, checkpointing, artifact mutation, and agent-directed control.

features: parent/child task and artifact digest binding
monotonic artifact version and lineage depth

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane receipt overhead; excludes task creation, artifact mutation, agents, tools, network, storage, models, and kernel scheduling latency

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the artifact-lineage module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged memory-promotion release

limitations: The contract records refinement admission evidence and does not create the child task or mutate the artifact store.
Acceptance evidence, task state, artifact state, lineage digests, and scope claims are caller-supplied and require trusted collection and enforcement for production.

The benchmark measures local Python control-plane receipt overhead and excludes actual durable storage, distributed coordination, artifact transfer, agents, tools, models, network, and kernel scheduler performance.
The real-task validation is a deterministic local fixture and does not establish artifact quality, general intelligence, browser autonomy, robotics, or production agent efficacy.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
